title: How to write an email to a potential advisor?
en:
How to write an email to a potential advisor?

It's the time of the year when faculty receives overwhelmingly many emails from prospective students. 

But most of them are poorly written. 😱

Some simple tips to make yours stand out. 👇

title: How to write an email to a potential advisor?
en:
*Write a distinct subject line*

Every email has the subject line "Prospective PhD Student for Fall 2024". 

Write something special about YOU, specific skills, experiences, or achievements.

title: How to write an email to a potential advisor?
en:
*Personalize your email*

Could not emphasize this enough! If you cannot personalize your email, don't send it.

❌ "I am deeply inspired by [two random papers I grab from your webpage]."

✅ "I ran the code of [your paper] and found an interesting failure case. My idea is ..."

title: How to write an email to a potential advisor?
en:
*Lead with values*

❌ "I am very interested ... I want to grow ... I want to get the experiences... I have so many prior experiences ... me, me, me, me, ME, ME, ME!"  

✅ "Here is what I can contribute to your team. I can do this bc my experience/skills on blah blah blah."

title: How to write an email to a potential advisor?
en:
*Avoid unnecessary questions*

❓ What's my chance of getting admitted? 
-> It depends.

❓ Will you be taking new students?
-> It's on my website.

❓ Can you interview me?
-> Ain't nobody got time for that.
How to invite yourself to give a talk?

title: How to invite yourself to give a talk?
en:
How to invite yourself to give a talk?

If you are not already famous, come from a famous university, or have a famous advisor, you will almost surely NOT be invited to give a talk.

You can be cynical and complain about it every day...

OR, you can invite yourself!

title: How to invite yourself to give a talk?
en:
*How?*

It's all about connections. 

But as a junior student, you don't know many established faculty elsewhere. What can you do?

1⃣ Leverage your advisor's connection. 
2⃣ Your contacts (mostly students in another university).
3⃣ Cold emails.

Let's break it down.

title: How to invite yourself to give a talk?
en:
*Leverage your advisor's connection*

Ask your advisor which groups would be interested in learning about your research. Ask if they can help refer you. 

A good advisor always looks for ways to promote you whenever they can. They will happily do so if you ask.

title: How to invite yourself to give a talk?
en:
*Your contacts*

Feel scared to contact PIs you never met? Shoot an email to your (student) contacts. They can ask around and help set up the talk. 

Many of those talks/seminars are organized by students anyway. 

How do you know more people? 

Check out https://x.com/jbhuang0604/status/1517352789780934656

title: How to invite yourself to give a talk?
en:
How to network at a conference?

Many students will be attending their first-ever *in-person* conference this year. How exciting! 🤩

Some tips on making the best of attending a conference. 🧵

title: How to invite yourself to give a talk?
en:
*Cold emails*

For many people, this can be very daunting. 

But it's not that bad. 

Most people who receive the self-invited talk requests would gladly help host it.

Here is a template if you need one.

title: How to invite yourself to give a talk?
en:
*Jump before you're ready*

"I will give a talk when I am ready."

No, you will never be ready. It's just your brain trying to convince yourself to stay in your comfort zone. 

Preparing a talk is an excellent way to organize your work. It's also great to connect & get feedback.

title: How to invite yourself to give a talk?
en:
Hope this helps! 

Giving a good talk not only helps clarify your vision, but also builds lasting connections with others (and of course, advances your career).

Best of luck!
How to get people to know you?

title: How to get people to know you?
en:
Got several requests for advice on academic job search. 🎓

People often seek advice on CV & research/teaching/diversity statements. 

Yes, those are important. BUT from my experience, the single most important factor of the search:

Do they ALREADY KNOW YOU (before you apply)?

title: How to get people to know you?
en:
*Why is that?*

Faculty are busy creatures. Most faculty probably won't have time to read through all your CV/statements in great detail and THEN objectively form their opinions on your application.

It's unfortunate, but true.

title: How to get people to know you?
en:
*Unfair advantages*

If they already know you, either 
- via your research (award-winning, salient papers), or 
- via your famous advisor giving many invited talks here and there,

you get a HUGE advantage over others.

(bc you become a *safe* candidate to invite for interview.)

title: How to get people to know you?
en:
*Bias toward prominent institutes*

This is probably why academia "is characterized by universally extreme inequality in faculty production."

https://x.com/jbhuang0604/status/1637151669732491264

title: How to get people to know you?
en:
Student: I want to pursue an academic career. Do I have to do a PhD at a top university?

Me: Of course not! You will be evaluated based on the quality of your work, NOT the university prestige.

Student: But all the faculty candidates we interviewed are from top places.

Me: https://t.co/NMpw8Kd5tU

title: How to get people to know you?
en:
*So what should I do?*

Not coming from high-prestige places, no famous advisor, no paper awards? 

That's okay. 

Just make yourself KNOWN to other people.

title: How to get people to know you?
en:
*How?*

1⃣ Share your work in public and build an audience. 

2⃣ Learn to sell your work well. 

3⃣ Invite yourself to give invited talks.

I found these three strategies super helpful to mitigate the disadvantages.

title: How to get people to know you?
en:
Hope this helps and GOOD LUCK with your job search!

Each action item can probably be a thread itself...maybe some other time. 

Stay tuned!
How to schedule your defense?

title: How to schedule your defense?
en:
How to schedule your thesis defense?

So you think publishing top-tier papers is hard? Wait until you need to schedule your prelim/defense!

Some common mistakes and tips:

title: How to schedule your defense?
en:
*Generation vs Verification?*

Do NOT send when2meet/doodle to everyone with so many options.

You are effectively asking busy academics to cave out 10 mins to label ALL of their available time and put all of them *on hold* for you.

Ain't nobody got time for that.

title: How to schedule your defense?
en:
*Use verification instead*

Instead of asking people to generate all the available time slots, ask them to verify if certain time slots work for them. 

Make sure to remove hard constraints like courses/travel. 

Verification is waaaay easier. 

You will get responses in no time!

title: How to schedule your defense?
en:
*Be specific*

Don’t ask for general time slots during a week. Academics are creatures that value freedom. 

Their calendar is a hot mess! Interviews, talks, travel, committee meetings on forming another committee. Every week is different.

Ask for specific date/time instead.

title: How to schedule your defense?
en:
*Sent calendar invite right away*

Get a consensus? Congrats! 

Send the calendar invite immediately and secure the confirmation. Academics are like goldfish and will forget about it as soon as they archive your email thread.

Anything that is not on their calendar does not exist!
How to manage your time?

title: How to manage your time?
en:
For the first time in five years, I have a full-time work schedule. I thought I will trivially be 3-4 times more productive, but it turns out managing time well is so damn challenging. 😬

After watching productivity videos to procrastinate, here are what I found useful. 🧵

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Eat that frog*

If you have to eat a frog, make it the very first task you do in your day. If you have to eat three frogs a day, do not start with the small one.

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Have a plan*

If you have no idea what you will be doing 2:30 PM next Wed, you are doing it wrong. It's okay to be flexible and change the plan, but make sure that you have a plan to start with.

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Do what you are doing*

Be aware of what the task you are doing at the present time. Multitasking is simply an illusion of rapid context switching.

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Treat time as space*

Make EVERYTHING you plan to do as a calendar entry (including planning the calendar) and do it at that time. Check out @deviparikh's excellent blog post. 

https://deviparikh.medium.com/calendar-in-stead-of-to-do-lists-9ada86a512dd

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Use interrupt coalescing* 

Group and defer interruptions (e.g., emails, slack messages, twitter feeds) according to their urgency. Allocate a specific time slot in a day to address these interruptions.

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Break your day down into short time chunks*

Get a timer/app, work on your task for 25 mins. Take a 5 min break and repeat. (Pomodoro Technique)

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Learn to say no*

Before accepting any new tasks, ask yourself 
• Why should I do it? 
• What happens if I don't do it?

Pro tip: Create a "no" folder to save the things you said no. Celebrate how much time you get back in your life.

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Give up precise task prioritization*

Sometimes you may be spending more time ranking the tasks than actually doing it.

title: How to manage your time?
en:
*Touch each email exactly once*

Open an email, skim through it, and make a quick decision (reply/archive/allocate a time slot). Keep your inbox zero.

title: How to manage your time?
en:
Any tips/advices on time management are very welcome! 

(Procrastinating with this twitter thread...)
How to develop a productive routine?

title: How to develop a productive routine?
en:
How to develop a productive routine?

When transiting from structured learning environments (e.g., courses) to unstructured ones (e.g., research), developing a productive routine and managing their time well are critical for productivity. 

Sharing some hacks I found useful! 👇

title: How to develop a productive routine?
en:
*168 hours a week*

There is time. 🕘

Thinking the time you have in terms of a week (as oppose a day) gives you new perspective on how much you could achieve.

🧮168 - (8 hrs sleep * 7 days) - (40 hrs work / week) = 72 hrs!

Make the best use of your time on what you care most!
